arxiv-2012-09036.title: Improved StyleGAN Embedding: Where are the Good Latents? Journal: TOG CCS: Computing methodologies Image processing CCS: Computing methodologies Reconstruction CCS: Computing methodologies Neural networks
arxiv-2012-09036.creator: Peihao Zhu, Rameen Abdal, Yipeng Qin, John Femiani, Peter Wonka
arxiv-2012-09036.description: Abstract . StyleGAN is able to produce photorealistic images that are almost indistinguishable from real photos. The reverse problem of finding an embedding for a given image poses a challenge. Embeddings that reconstruct an image well are not always robust to editing operations.

arxiv-2106-07212.title: Imaging the breaking of electrostatic dams in graphene for ballistic and viscous fluids
arxiv-2106-07212.creator: Zachary J. Krebs, Wyatt A. Behn, Songci Li, Keenan J. Smith, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Alex Levchenko, Victor W. Brar
arxiv-2106-07212.description: Abstract The flow of charge carriers in materials can, under some circumstances, mimic the flow of viscous fluids. In order to visualize the consequences of such effects, new methodologies must be developed that can probe the quasiparticle flow profile with nm-scale resolution as the geometric parameters of the system are continuously evolved.

arxiv-2108-02653.title: Practices of public procurement and the risk of corrupt behavior before and after the government transition in México
arxiv-2108-02653.creator: Andrea Falcón-Cortés, Andrés Aldana, Hernán Larralde
arxiv-2108-02653.description: Abstract Abstract: Corruption has a significant impact on economic growth, democracy, and inequality. It has sever consequences at the human level. Public procurement, where public resources are used to purchase goods or services from the private sector, are particularly susceptible to corrupt practices.

arxiv-2110-12000.title: Bank transactions embeddings help to uncover current macroeconomics
arxiv-2110-12000.creator: 1 st Maria Begicheva, 2 nd Alexey Zaytsev
arxiv-2110-12000.description: Abstract Macroeconomic indexes are of high importance for banks: many risk-control decisions utilize these indexes. A typical workflow of these indexes evaluation is costly and protracted, with a lag between the actual date and available index being a couple of months. Banks predict such indexes now using autoregressive models to make decisions in a rapidly changing environment.

arxiv-2203-02338.title: Circularly polarized periodic gravitational wave and the Pais-Uhlenbeck oscillator
arxiv-2203-02338.creator: Mahmut Elbistan
arxiv-2203-02338.description: Abstract The “Bargmann framework” allows us to prove the equivalence of the Pais-Uhlenbeck oscillator with a spin-zero particle in a circularly polarized periodic gravitational wave. Pushing forward the symmetries (which include Carroll symmetry) of the latter, we derive conserved charges for the Pais-Uhlenbeck oscillator.

arxiv-2210-03135.title: The hidden side of cosmic star formation at z z > > 3
arxiv-2210-03135.creator: M.-Y. Xiao, D. Elbaz, C. Gómez-Guijarro, L. Leroy, L.-J. Bing, E. Daddi, B. Magnelli, M. Franco, L. Zhou, M. Dickinson, T. Wang, W. Rujopakarn, G. E. Magdis, E. Treister, H. Inami, R. Demarco, M. T. Sargent, X. Shu, J. S. Kartaltepe, D. M. Alexander, M. Béthermin, F. Bournaud, L. Ciesla, H. C. Fergu
arxiv-2210-03135.description: Abstract Our current understanding of the cosmic star formation history at z > 3 z>3 is primarily based on UV-selected galaxies (Lyman-break galaxies, i.e., LBGs). Recent studies of H H -dropouts (HST-dark galaxies) have revealed that we may be missing a large proportion of star formation that is taking place in massive galaxies at z > 3 z>3 .

arxiv-2210-10885.title: New EoR Power Spectrum Limits From MWA Phase II Using the Delay Spectrum Method and Novel Systematic Rejection 2021 New EoR Power Spectrum Limits From MWA Phase II Using the Delay Spectrum Method and Novel Systematic Rejection – 4
arxiv-2210-10885.creator: Matthew Kolopanis, Jonathan C. Pober, Daniel C. Jacobs, Samantha McGraw
arxiv-2210-10885.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Matthew Kolopanis, Jonathan C. Pober, Daniel C. Jacobs, Samantha McGraw. We present an analysis of Epoch of Reionization data from Phase II of the Murchison Widefield Array using the simpleDS delay spectrum pipeline. Prior work analyzed the same observations using the FHD/ ε \varepsilon ppsilon imaging pipeline, and so the present analysis represents the first time that both principal types of 21 cm cosmology power spectrum estimation approaches have been applied to the same data set.

arxiv-2309-13821.title: An ALMA-resolved view of 7000 au Protostellar Gas Ring around the Class I source CrA-IRS 2 as a possible sign of magnetic flux advection astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , CASA ( CASA Team et al. 2022 )
arxiv-2309-13821.creator: Kazuki Tokuda, Naofumi Fukaya, Kengo Tachihara, Mitsuki Omura, Naoto Harada, Shingo Nozaki, Ayumu Shoshi, Masahiro N. Machida
arxiv-2309-13821.description: Abstract Transferring a significant fraction of the magnetic flux from a dense cloud core is essential in the star formation process. A ring-like structure produced by magnetic flux loss has been predicted theoretically, but no observational identification has been presented.

arxiv-2310-02814.title: Graph-based Simultaneous Localization and Bias Tracking A. Venus and E. Leitinger are with the Signal Processing and Speech Communication Laboratory, Graz University of Technology, Graz, Austria, and the Christian Doppler Laboratory for Location-aware Electronic Systems (e-mail: (erik.leitinger,a.ve
arxiv-2310-02814.creator: Alexander Venus, , Erik Leitinger, , Stefan Tertinek, Florian Meyer , and Klaus Witrisal,
arxiv-2310-02814.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Alexander Venus, , Erik Leitinger, , Stefan Tertinek, Florian Meyer , and Klaus Witrisal,. We present a factor graph formulation and particle-based sum-product algorithm for robust localization and tracking in multipath-prone environments. The proposed sequential algorithm jointly estimates the mobile agent’s position together with a time-varying number of mpc . The mpc are represented by “delay biases” corresponding to the offset between los ( los ) component delay and the respective delays of all detectable mpc .

arxiv-2401-11341.title: Sensory adaptation in a continuum model of bacterial chemotaxis - working range, cost-accuracy relation, and coupled systems
arxiv-2401-11341.creator: Vansh Kharbanda, Benedikt Sabass
arxiv-2401-11341.description: Abstract Sensory adaptation enables organisms to adjust their perception in a changing environment. A paradigm is bacterial chemotaxis, where the output activity of chemoreceptors is adapted to different baseline concentrations via receptor methylation. The range of internal receptor states limits the stimulus magnitude to which these systems can adapt.

Squassina is member of Gruppo Nazionale per l’Analisi Matematica, la Probabilita e le loro Applicazioni (GNAMPA) of the Istituto Nazionale

arxiv-2403-18014.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Liejun Shen, Marco Squassina. arxiv-2412-19129.title: The effect of grain boundary misorientation on hydrogen flux using a phase-field based diffusion and trapping model Published in: Advanced Engineering Materials 26(22)(2024): 2401561
arxiv-2412-19129.creator: Abdelrahman Hussein, Byungki Kim, Kim Verbeken, Tom Depover
arxiv-2412-19129.description: Abstract Understanding hydrogen-grain boundary (GB) interactions is critical to the analysis of hydrogen embrittlement in metals. This work presents a mesoscale fully kinetic model to investigate the effect of GB misorientation on hydrogen diffusion and trapping using phase-field based representative volume elements (RVEs).

arxiv-2505-08706.title: Big Data and the Computational Social Science of Entrepreneurship and Innovation Publication type: research-article DOI: 10.1515/9783111085722-019
arxiv-2505-08706.creator: Li.Ningzi Lilabel=e1]ningzi@uchicago.edu \bio bio1, Lai.Shiyang Lailabel=e2]shiyanglai@uchicago.edu \bio bio2, Evans.James Evans f2 label=e3]jevans@uchicago.edu \bio bio3
arxiv-2505-08706.description: Abstract As large-scale social data explode and machine-learning methods evolve, scholars of entrepreneurship and innovation face new research opportunities but also unique challenges. This chapter discusses the difficulties of leveraging large-scale data to identify technological and commercial novelty, document new venture origins, and forecast competition between new technologies and commercial forms.

arxiv-2505-17452.title: Deblending overlapping galaxies in DECaLS using Transformer-Based algorithm: a method combining multiple bands and data types
arxiv-2505-17452.creator: Ran Zhang, Meng Liu, Zhenping Yi, Hao Yuan, Zechao Yang, Yude Bu, Xiaoming Kong, Chenglin Jia, Yuchen Bi, Yusheng Zhang, Nan Li
arxiv-2505-17452.description: Abstract In large-scale galaxy surveys, particularly deep ground-based photometric studies, galaxy blending was inevitable. Such blending posed a potential primary systematic uncertainty for upcoming surveys. Current deblenders predominantly depended on analytical modeling of galaxy profiles, facing limitations due to inflexible and imprecise models.

arxiv-2508-13901.title: Multimodal Data Storage and Retrieval for Embodied AI: A Survey
arxiv-2508-13901.creator: Yihao Lu, Hao Tang
arxiv-2508-13901.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yihao Lu, Hao Tang. Embodied AI (EAI) agents continuously interact with the physical world, generating vast, heterogeneous multimodal data streams that traditional management systems are ill-equipped to handle. In this survey, we first systematically evaluate five storage architectures (Graph Databases, Multi-Model Databases, Data Lakes, Vector Databases, and Time-Series Databases), focusing on their suitability for addressing EAI’s core requirements, including physical grounding, low-latency access, and dynamic scalability.

arxiv-2511-07744.title: VectorSynth: Fine-Grained Satellite Image Synthesis with Structured Semantics
arxiv-2511-07744.creator: Daniel Cher, Brian WeiSrikumar SastryNathan JacobsWashington University in St. Louis {cher, b.j.wei, s.sastry, jacobsn}@wustl.edu
arxiv-2511-07744.description: Abstract We introduce VectorSynth, a diffusion-based framework for pixel-accurate satellite image synthesis conditioned on polygonal geographic annotations with semantic attributes. Unlike prior text- or layout-conditioned models, VectorSynth learns dense cross-modal correspondences that align imagery and semantic vector geometry, enabling fine-grained, spatially grounded edits.

arxiv-2511-13604.title: Long-range entanglement and quantum correlations in a multi-frequency comb system
arxiv-2511-13604.creator: Sahil Pontula 1,2,3, Debasmita Banerjee 4, Marin Soljačić 1,3, Yannick Salamin 4
arxiv-2511-13604.description: Abstract Frequency combs are multimode photonic systems that underlie countless precision sensing and metrology applications. Since their invention over two decades ago, numerous efforts have pushed frequency combs to broader bandwidths and more stable operation. More recently, quantum squeezing and entanglement have been explored in single frequency comb systems for quantum advantages in sensing and signal multiplexing.

arxiv-2602-18772.title: From Ponzi Schemes to Benign Investment Dynamics: modelling Collapse, Stability, and a Path to Sustainability Journal: Finance Research Open
arxiv-2602-18772.creator: Bernhard R. Parodi
arxiv-2602-18772.description: Abstract The population and capital dynamics of three stylized investment systems are mathematically described using discrete-time difference equations with closed-form solutions. The models share a common capital budget equation but differ in their demographic laws, which are geometric, quasi-logistic, or epidemiologic (SIR-based).

europmc-pmc6406315.title: Reducing Racial Inequities in Health: Using What We Already Know to Take Action.
europmc-pmc6406315.creator: Williams DR, Cooper LA.
europmc-pmc6406315.description: This paper provides an overview of the scientific evidence pointing to critically needed steps to reduce racial inequities in health. First, it argues that communities of opportunity should be developed to minimize some of the adverse impacts of systemic racism. These are...

frus-1861-d61.title: Mr. Seward to Mr. Adams.
frus-1861-d61.creator: U.S. Department of State
frus-1861-d61.source: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
frus-1861-d61.description: FRUS Message of the President of the United States to the Two Houses of Congress, at , Document 61, dated 21 July 1861: Mr. Seward to Mr. Adams.

pmc-10613353.title: Should additional value elements be included in cost-effectiveness analysis in pharmacoeconomic evaluation: a novel commentary
pmc-10613353.creator: Lihua Sun, Shiqi Li, Xiaochen Peng
pmc-10613353.description: In recent years, international academics recognized that quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) may not always fully capture the benefits produced by an intervention, and considered incorporating additional elements of value into cost-effectiveness analysis (CEA). Examples of these elements are adherence-improving factors, insurance value, value of hope, and real option value, which form the “value flower”.

pmc-11435394.title: Phenylethanol Glycoside from Cistanche tubulosa Attenuates BSA-Induced Liver Fibrosis in Rats by Modulating the Gut Microbiota–Liver Axis
pmc-11435394.creator: Xinxin Qi, Hongguang Sun, Jincun Liu, Meili Cong, Xinxuan Zhang, Yuxin Yan, Zhaolin Xia, Tao Liu, Jun Zhao, Angel Josabad Alonso-Castro
pmc-11435394.description: This study aimed to investigate the effect of phenylethanol glycoside from Cistanche tubulosa (CPhGs) on the prevention of bovine serum albumin (BSA)-induced hepatic fibrosis in rats. Investigation of the mechanisms of the anti-hepatic fibrosis effect was focused on CPhGs’ influence on the “gut–liver” regulation, including the gut microbiota, intestinal barrier, systemic lipopolysaccharide (LPS) concentration, and LPS-related signaling pathway.

pmc-11494557.title: Opportunity for severe and critical COVID-19 pneumonia treatment with corticosteroids: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-11494557.creator: Fan Chen, Liang Zong, Yan Li, Huadong Zhu, Shengyong Xu, Jun Xu
pmc-11494557.description: BackgroundThe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has been the most significant infectious disease outbreak worldwide in the past 3 years, with the potential to progress to severe pneumonia and trigger systemic inflammatory response, posing a threat to human health and life.

pmc-11532473.title: Environmental factors and chronic kidney disease: a case-control study
pmc-11532473.creator: Mousa Ghelichi-Ghojogh, Mohammad fararouei, Mozhgan Seif, Maryam Pakfetrat
pmc-11532473.description: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a non-communicable disease that includes a range of different physiological disorders causing abnormal renal function and progressive decline in the glomerular filtration rate (GFR). This study aimed to investigate the associations of several Environmental factors with CKD in the Iranian population.

pmc-11639903.title: Novel PCR-Based Technology for the Detection of Sunflower in Edible and Used Cooking Oils
pmc-11639903.creator: Tamara Kutateladze, Kakha Karchkhadze, Kakha Bitskinashvili, Boris Vishnepolsky, Tata Ninidze, David Mikeladze, Nelly Datukishvili, Susana Casal
pmc-11639903.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Reliable detection of sunflower (Helianthus annuus) in edible and used cooking oil (UCO) is crucial for the sustainable production of food and biodiesel. In this study, a variety of sunflower oils (crude, cold pressed, extra virgin, refined, and UCO) were examined using different methods of DNA extraction and PCR amplification to develop an efficient technology for the identification of sunflower in oils.

pmc-12331820.title: Autonomic Disequilibrium at Rest in Autistic Children and Adults
pmc-12331820.creator: Maria Rosa Bufo, Marco Guidotti, Mathieu Lemaire, Joëlle Malvy, Emmanuelle Houy-Durand, Frédérique Bonnet-Brilhault, Frédéric Briend, Nadia Aguillon-Hernandez, Claire Wardak
pmc-12331820.description: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) symptoms have been proposed to be linked to Autonomic Nervous System (ANS) atypical functioning, in particular sympathetic hyper-arousal and parasympathetic under-activation. The objective of this study was to characterize autonomic functioning at rest in autistic and neurotypical children and adults.

pmc-13117445.title: Effect of Vinblastine Timing on Skin Graft Healing in a Rat Model
pmc-13117445.creator: Eren Tuncer, Elif Gündeş Alten, Aytaç Alten, Erol Kozanoğlu, Şule Öztürk Sarı, Ufuk Emekli
pmc-13117445.description: Background and Objectives: Chemotherapeutic agents are known to disrupt wound healing; however, the influence of administration timing on skin graft repair remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to investigate the time-dependent effects of vinblastine exposure on full-thickness skin graft healing in a rat model. Materials and Methods: Twenty-four female Wistar albino rats were allocated into four groups (n = 6).

pmc-13378963.title: Prevalence and factors associated with treatment delay among colorectal cancer patients at Mulago National Referral Hospital and the Uganda Cancer Institute: A cross-sectional study
pmc-13378963.creator: Brian Kasagga, Paul Ssempebwa, Godfrey Kikuba, Flavius E. Egbe, Peace Caroline Nsodi, Joanne Kayaga, Emmanuel Alex Elobu, Paul Okeny, Aloysius Gonzaga Mubuuke, Aloysius Gonzaga Mubuuke, Aloysius Gonzaga Mubuuke, Aloysius Gonzaga Mubuuke, Aloysius Gonzaga Mubuuke
pmc-13378963.description: BackgroundColorectal cancer (CRC) is an important cause of morbidity and mortality in Uganda. Timely treatment initiation is critical for outcomes, yet delays are common. This study assessed treatment delays and associated factors among CRC patients at Mulago National Referral Hospital (MNRH) and the Uganda Cancer Institute (UCI).

pmc-13443735.title: Making every test count: Insights from a test kit efficiency audit
pmc-13443735.creator: Amy O. Strydom, Mpho R. Maphayi, Chemedzai Chikomba
pmc-13443735.description: BackgroundClinical laboratories face increasing demand for testing while operating within constrained budgets, necessitating efficient resource utilisation. Test kit efficiency, a key parameter in automated laboratories, refers to the appropriate use of reagent kits in a manner that minimises non-billable tests per kit.
